coverage.why: Every venue calendar page JamBase serves loads the venue's FULL future schedule on one request (no 'load more' or date pager was ever shown, even for Moody Center's ~2 dozen dates running to Jul 2027) -- so one fetch per venue was a complete read, not a first page. Direct curl was blocked outright (HTTP 403, Cloudflare 'cf-mitigated: challenge' -- a managed bot challenge, not a rate limit) on every path tried, including robots.txt-permitted ones; firecrawl_scrape with the default 'basic' proxy got clean 200s throughout, so the whole study runs on firecrawl. Two venues (The Parish, and the electronic room Summit) needed extra digging: The Parish has no JamBase venue page at all under any of the slugs or search terms I tried (confirmed via firecrawl_search restricted to jambase.com/venue -- the only hit was the unrelated 'St Austin Catholic Parish'), and Summit's page exists (/venue/summit-rooftop-austin-tx, capacity 500, address matches) but currently lists zero upcoming shows.

cityWide.note: JamBase's Austin-area listing is paginated (18+ pages for the 'Austin' city page alone, more again for 'Austin Area', with no visible total count or date-range filter that maps cleanly to a rolling 30-day window) and mixes our 17-ish core venues with dozens of others across the metro (Cedar Park, San Marcos, Dripping Springs, Round Rock, etc. all show up under 'Austin Area'). Getting an honest 30-day count would mean paging through and de-duplicating several list pages, which the firecrawl budget for this task didn't leave room for beyond the one page fetched to harvest venue links. Recommend a dedicated pass (or the JamBase Data API this page advertises at data.jambase.com) if the city-wide count specifically is needed.

linkBehavior: Every event page's primary 'Get Tickets' button is JamBase's own affiliate-network redirect, never a bare link to the ticketer. The Ticketmaster link is wrapped as an Impact/awin-style affiliate URL (`https://ticketmaster.evyy.net/c/252938/271177/4272?u=<url-encoded real Ticketmaster event URL>&utm_medium=affiliate&utm_source=jambase&subid1=show&subid2=<show-slug>`) -- the real destination is recoverable by decoding the `u=` param. AXS is the one exception seen: it links straight to axs.com with just a `?cid=usaffjambase` tracking param appended, no redirector domain. Below the primary ticketer, every page also lists 4-6 resale marketplaces (StubHub, TickPick, Gametime, SeatGeek, Vivid Seats, Viagogo), each also wrapped in its own affiliate-network redirector (stubhub.prf.hn, tickpick.dgrk2e.net, hnyj8s.net for Gametime, seatgeek.pxf.io, vivid-seats.pxf.io, viagogo.prf.hn) and each also tagged utm_source=jambase.
